title.analysis: Authentic title "How Banks Actually Make Money Off You (10 Things Most People Miss)" is an exposé-style list promise. The script covers about ten themes (savings yields, net interest margin, money creation, credit cards, risk pricing, securities-backed borrowing, offshore banking, mortgages, deposit insurance, FX fees) but never numbers them, and its closing "10 secrets" line is the only explicit list reference.

script.opening_words: You walk into your bank on a Tuesday morning to deposit your paycheck. The teller smiles, processes your deposit, and hands you a receipt. You feel good. Your money is safe, growing steadily, and the bank is looking out for your financial future. Right? Wrong. Uh, what if I told you that in the next 20 minutes, I'm going to shatter every assumption you've ever had about how banks actually work and what they're really doing with your hard-earned cash.
script.ending_words: about how you approach every financial decision you make. So, there you have it. 10 secrets that banks would prefer you never learned. If this video changed how you think about money and banking, share it with someone who needs to hear this. Hit that subscribe button if you want more content that exposes the hidden mechanics of wealth. And remember, the best defense against being played is understanding the
script.analysis: Full 23746 canonical characters read. A single-narrator banking exposé: hook about a teller, savings yields versus inflation, deposits as loans and net interest margin, money creation and the 2020 zero reserve requirement, card profitability and "deadbeats", risk-based pricing, securities-backed borrowing and stepped-up basis, offshore banking as a cross-subsidy, mortgage amortisation, a repeated fractional-reserve section with bank runs, FDIC and moral hazard, 2008, FX fees, financial literacy, and a conclusion. Several factual errors (FDIC per account, $600,000 mortgage total, FX example) and a leaked "continuation of the script" line point to weakly edited generated text; the stored ending is truncated.
beat_map: Hook: depositing a paycheck; promise to shatter assumptions.
Deposits as loans; net interest margin.
Fractional reserve again; bank runs; FDIC and Fed backstops.
Financial literacy and product complexity; CDs vs bonds.
